items.cite: Rae Linda Brown, *The Heart of a Woman: The Life and Music of Florence B. Price*, edited and with a foreword by Guthrie P. Ramsey Jr. (University of Illinois Press, 2020).
items.note: The standard study of how Price’s training, teaching, family responsibilities and Chicago career relate to her major compositions; it draws on archival and interview research and includes musical examples.

items.cite: Samantha Ege, *South Side Impresarios: How Race Women Transformed Chicago’s Classical Music Scene* (University of Illinois Press, 2024).
items.note: On the teachers, patrons, organisers and women’s networks that supported classical music on the South Side around Price, Margaret Bonds and Nora Holt. Useful on the work behind a public première.

items.cite: Florence Price, *Symphonies Nos. 1 and 3*, edited by Rae Linda Brown and Wayne Shirley, Music of the United States of America 19 (A-R Editions, 2008).
items.note: Provides the full orchestral scores and English critical commentary for tracing the brass hymn, Juba movements and editorial decisions.

items.cite: Michael Lively, ‘Multi-Linear Continuity and “Songs to the Dark Virgin” by Florence Price [1888–1953]’, *College Music Symposium* 63, no. 1 (2023), doi:10.18177/sym.2023.63.sr.11581.
items.note: Examines how piano figures, recurring dissonances and competing harmonic readings interact with Hughes’s poem. The article’s title gives an older birth year; its text gives 1887.
